name: SIGINT
standfirst: Security research and practitioner news, scored for novelty and actionability.
colophon: sigint.wtf — the correct response to most of these CVEs. Scored by machine against a hand-written rubric; ranking is opinion, not fact.

items.title: Ruby 4.0 Universal RCE Deserialization Gadget Chain
items.dek: Universal Ruby deserialization gadget chain enables RCE; requires immediate review if Ruby is in the SDLC dependency tree.
items.unproven: depends on whether reader's codebase uses vulnerable deserialization patterns; exploitation conditions not yet confirmed in production environments

items.title: Does Fixing Break Security? An Empirical Study of Security Degradation in Iterative LLM-Driven Infrastructure-as-Code Repair
items.dek: 13.8% of LLM-repaired IaC scenarios regress on at least one CIS check while fixing others; iterative loops do not monotonically improve security.
items.unproven: IaC-Eval benchmark only; unclear if regression pattern holds across other validation frameworks or real production workflows.

items.title: Labels Are Not Endpoints: Treatment Leakage and Construct Validity in MCP Agent Security Evaluation
items.dek: Agent security evaluations suffer treatment leakage in labeling; audit of benchmark campaign corrects 58 mislabeled attack records, zero confirmed attacks in corrected dataset.
items.unproven: limited to one preserved campaign; whether labeling flaws are systematic across other published agent security benchmarks unknown; methodology not yet adopted by other evaluators

items.title: LLM-Assisted Dynamic Threat Analysis for Attacker-Reachable Software Weaknesses in Autonomous Vehicles
items.dek: LLMs generate 3,700 test harnesses for safety-critical weaknesses in Autoware; 64% compile first-attempt, 80% failures are dependency wiring.
items.unproven: One codebase (Autoware), no evidence that generated harnesses find exploitable vulnerabilities missed by existing SAST or fuzzing pipelines.

items.title: Operationalizing Cyber Threat Intelligence with GraphRAG
items.dek: GraphRAG-based detection rule generation sustained 100% alert rate after IP/domain/hash rotation versus 29% for vector-similarity retrieval on one APT28 report.
items.unproven: single case study; generalization to other threat reports, detection engineering workflows, and false-positive trade-offs not established; comparison limited to one baseline approach.

items.title: InSPECtor: Improving SLEIGH Processor Specification Veracity via Proxy
items.dek: Differential testing of SLEIGH processor specifications against hardware references uncovered over 38,920 discrepancies in x86-64, AArch64, ARM, RISC-V, and MSP430.
items.unproven: impact of discrepancies on real-world disassembly, decompilation, or vulnerability analysis not quantified; whether findings force specification corrections or tool mitigations remains unclear.

items.title: ATOBench: Tracing How Autonomous Penetration-Testing Agents Verify Vulnerabilities When Target Evidence Lies
items.dek: ATOBench makes autonomous penetration-testing agent verification observable by injecting response transformations at runtime and tracking report construction against deceptive evidence.
items.unproven: evaluation on five model routes only; generalization to production red-team workflows and real exploitation scenarios not established; whether findings apply to agents deployed without observable verification loops unclear.

items.title: Dissecting Software Graphs: Structural Insights for Driver-Guided Fuzzing
items.dek: Multi-driver fuzzing on 27 OSS-Fuzz projects covers 27.9% more call-graph nodes and 73.5% more CFG edges than single-driver baseline.
items.unproven: results on 854 driver configurations from open-source C/C++ only; whether multi-driver strategy improves finding exploitable bugs versus coverage metrics; applicability to closed-source or Java/Python codebases unclear

items.title: Beyond Source: An Empirical Study of Python Bytecode Security Risks
items.dek: 7,388 PyPI artifacts contain bytecode; 228k .pyc files found, decompilers fail on adversarial bytecode, driving 17 distinct robustness failures.
items.unproven: decompiler emission measured, not verified functional equivalence; whether source-level reproduction covers all bytecode attack vectors; impact on supply-chain risk in production Python dependency trees not quantified

items.title: A Commitment-Based Hybrid Post-Quantum Cryptographic Model for Multi-File Cloud Storage
items.dek: Batch commitment over hybrid post-quantum signatures reduces per-file signing cost from O(n) to O(1) in cloud storage.
items.unproven: evaluation limited to commodity client platform; integration cost with existing cloud APIs and key rotation workflows not measured; performance on competing batch-signature schemes not established.

items.title: For the love of god stop using CPU limits in Kubernetes
items.dek: Kubernetes CPU limits often misconfig and harm stability; informs platform hardening this quarter if reader runs K8s.
items.unproven: scoped to CPU limits only; does not cover memory, I/O, or network resource controls

items.title: Person Hides Prompt Injection in Legal Filing Telling AI to Side with Them
items.dek: Prompt injection embedded in legal document demonstrates an attack surface in LLM-assisted review workflows.
items.unproven: whether production legal AI systems lack defenses against this; applicability to agents in SDLC pipelines

items.title: Experimental Quantum Key Distribution in an Indefinite Causal Order
items.dek: Photonic quantum BB84 variant using indefinite causal order detects eavesdropping without disclosing key material.
items.unproven: lab-scale proof-of-concept only; post-quantum cryptography and quantum key distribution are outside reader's security-SDLC remit

items.title: Exponential quantum advantage for learning signals with a single qubit
items.dek: Single-qubit coupling to classical sensors achieves 10⁷-fold measurement reduction for signal learning.
items.unproven: Scalability beyond proof-of-concept demonstrations; generalization to real dark-matter and wireless systems.

items.title: Strong unitary designs in optimal depth and space
items.dek: Strong unitary designs achievable in logarithmic depth using only system qubits.
items.unproven: Experimental demonstration on real quantum hardware; overhead constants and noise resilience.

items.title: TopoIntent: Compiling Security Intent into Executable, Compliance-Checked Network Topologies
items.dek: LLM system compiles natural-language security intent into network topologies, checks against CIS Controls v8.1.2, exports to Mininet.
items.unproven: Evaluation benchmark constructed by authors; no evidence on real enterprise requirements or whether CIS-layer compliance ensures functional security.

items.title: Universal magic state concentration
items.dek: Fixed stabilizer protocol concentrates unknown non-stabilizer states to exact magic states using six copies.
items.unproven: Noise resilience; implementation on near-term processors; resource overhead versus existing distillation.

items.title: Formal Verification of Quantum Ancilla Safety
items.dek: Verification framework reduces dirty ancilla safety to 2m independent clean checks and algebraic commutativity.
items.unproven: no deployed integration into existing quantum compilers; repair routines handle only local single-qubit faults

items.title: InterSAGE: The Secure and Verifiable Interoperability Protocol for An Internet of Agents
items.dek: InterSAGE proposes identity, capability, trust negotiation, and audit layers for agent-to-agent interaction without consensus ledger.
items.unproven: no implementation, no deployment data, no comparison to competing agent security frameworks; kernel-mediated audit trail design and performance impact not demonstrated; compatibility with MCP, A2A, ANP only stated as intent.

items.title: RAGSieve: Self-Referenced Local Contrast for Knowledge-Poison Detection in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
items.dek: RAGSieve detects knowledge-poisoned retrieval documents via query-local and corpus-local contrast without requiring trusted references or global thresholds.
items.unproven: evaluation on three QA datasets only; attack success metric (67.4% baseline) not tied to real retrieval-augmented applications; false-positive cost at 5% clean-document removal not independently validated; scalability to production corpora unclear.

items.title: Beyond Handcrafted Security: Towards Self-Evolving Defense for LLM Agents
items.dek: HARD is a self-evolving runtime defense framework that automatically identifies intervention strategies for LLM agents and improves artifacts from observed failure traces.
items.unproven: no specification of how intervention strategies are enumerated or ranked; evaluation methodology and baselines not detailed; deployment feasibility and integration with production agent harnesses not addressed; whether autonomous evolution preserves interpretability of defenses unclear.

items.title: Understanding Backdoor Vulnerabilities in Vertical Federated Learning: The Gap Between Research and Practice
items.dek: Backdoor attacks on vertical federated learning fail under realistic constraints; prior research overlooks practical knowledge requirements and asymmetric information structures.
items.unproven: focus on threat characterization rather than new defense mechanisms; specific constraints that break prior work not formalized; mitigation strategies beyond identifying the gap not proposed.

items.title: Beyond Visual Evidence: Revealing and Mitigating Relational Privacy Leakage in Document MLLMs
items.dek: Document MLLMs leak correlated PII fields when visual evidence is missing, unlearning framework proposed to suppress leakage.
items.unproven: tested on three model families only; effectiveness of DRUF on production document-processing pipelines not demonstrated; whether field relations truly memorized versus learned from legitimate statistical correlation

items.title: Adversarial Robustness in Smishing Detection: A Comparative Analysis of Adversarial Fragility in Classical vs. Transformer-Based Detection Systems
items.dek: Classical ML models fail catastrophically on obfuscated smishing (RDR 0.988) while transformers resist better (RDR 0.351).
items.unproven: single dataset of 27k messages; low-resource attacker behaviors not necessarily representative of production smishing campaigns; transferability to deployed detection systems unclear

items.title: RealmEye: Virtual Machine Introspection for Arm CCA Realm VMs
items.dek: RealmEye enables VM introspection on Arm CCA Realm VMs via RMM, detecting rootkits without in-VM agent or hypervisor trust.
items.unproven: outside reader's remit; application security engineer does not operate cloud infrastructure, manage confidential VMs, or defend against kernel-level threats; relevant to infrastructure teams, not SDLC or secure development

noise.title: Going Dark, and the era of law enforcement hacking
noise.dek: Essay on law enforcement encryption workarounds and device access; rehashes known debates without new technical findings.
noise.unproven: entirely outside reader's remit; concerns policy and law enforcement capability, not application security engineering or SDLC

noise.title: Google is making private AI practical with homomorphic encryption
noise.dek: Google applies homomorphic encryption to inference; practical deployment timeline and performance overhead remain undisclosed.
noise.unproven: production viability, latency and cost at scale, whether constraints apply to the reader's AI agent use cases in SDLC

noise.title: Europe's scorched landscapes seen from space after summer heatwaves
noise.dek: Satellite imagery of European heat damage; climate reporting outside security scope.
